tasks.short: Develop and evaluate laboratory procedures and tests

steps.what: Define the specimen-analysis method change and verify its evaluation requirements
Perform the actual specimen experiments and verify captured observations and controls
Repeat specified precision, bias and comparison calculations on verified experiment data
Evaluate method suitability and decide the necessary procedure or test modifications
Write and check the revised laboratory procedure and supporting evaluation rationale
outputs: checked final revised procedure and evaluation

loop.purpose: Restate specified method changes and evaluation conclusions
loop.input: Existing procedure, technologist-authored exact changes and verified evaluation references
loop.output: Draft revised procedure with change and result references
loop.check: Technologist checks procedural meaning, omissions, specimen limits, controls, acceptance statements and every numerical claim against source results
loop.stop: Unsupported acceptance, changed control instruction or two failed drafts returns writing to manual
loop.why_not_simpler: Native controlled-document fields come first; limited variable rationale needs bounded restatement, not method design

steps.what: Review the exact final method revision, evaluation and intended clinical activation scope
inputs: checked final revised procedure and evaluation
outputs: approved procedure revision and activation scope

steps.what: Activate only the approved procedure revision for the specified laboratory scope
inputs: approved procedure revision and activation scope

tasks.design: Test native method-evaluation tables in the laboratory validation application in {OTHER}. Repeat selected statistics and use bounded restatement for the actual revised procedure in {DOCS}, retaining experiment work, scientific interpretation and final review before the separate clinical activation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated statistics and procedure restatement accompany experimental method development.
tasks.enabler_now: Fixed evaluation calculations and source-bound drafting can assist explicit work without choosing a clinical method.
tasks.still_hard: Establishing method suitability, failure modes and specimen limitations.
tasks.human_edge: Design the experiment and recognise when apparently acceptable statistics do not establish a usable test.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated calculation and procedure restatement with unchanged scientific and approval responsibilities.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: laboratory validation tools can repeat specified precision and comparison calculations; experimental design, method suitability and clinical activation need responsible laboratory review.

assumptions: Provisional workflow covers a genuine method revision through clinical activation. OTHER is the laboratory validation and controlled-method application. Focal technologist baseline is 96 points; 4 director-review points remain excluded other-role work. A research-only evaluation without activation must be reweighted.

The technologist verifies specimen/control ID, run, method version, result, unit, replicate and calculation specification in s1-s2. Experimental capture, extraction and missing-data repair remain counted; no free validated experimental dataset is assumed.

Native evaluation tables and controlled-document fields come first. Remove only 15 repeated manual calculation points and 1 of 10 procedure-restatement points. s4-s5 retain independent checks, substantive writing, draft repair and ordinary author saves; larger repair needs lower savings.

s6 director review follows the final complete revision and binds its exact version and clinical scope. Changes void approval. s7 is real method activation, not ordinary saving, and retains its full small time. Draft saves remain ungated.
unknowns: Existing statistical automation and repair effort
Actual method activation and review duties
research_questions: Replay one actual method modification and count data repair, independent checks and controlled activation separately.

incremental.description: Maintain validated calculation examples and procedure-draft checks

approvals.approved_version: s6 exact final method revision, evaluation references and clinical activation scope; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Remove 16 of 96 technologist points = 16.67%, less 1.5 upkeep = 15.17%. A novel assay supports only 3 points of compatible statistics and 0.3 routine procedure wording: 3.3/96*100 minus 1.5 = 1.94%; experimental and director work remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Cultivate specimens using the actual microbiological protocol and controls
Isolate microbial organisms and perform the required physical tests
Evaluate test observations and assist in identifying the microbial organisms
Enter and check the actual microbiology findings in the original laboratory record

tasks.design: Test native specimen-context defaults in the laboratory record application in {OTHER}. Reuse only the already verified specimen identifier in original working-record entry, retaining cultivation, isolation, tests, organism interpretation and complete record checking.
tasks.previous_blocker: A small repeated specimen-identifier entry accompanies predominantly physical laboratory work.
tasks.enabler_now: Native case context can reuse a selected specimen ID without generating microbiology findings.
tasks.still_hard: Obtaining reliable growth and interpreting organisms and controls correctly.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise contamination, unusual growth and inconclusive findings.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less repeated identifier entry with unchanged laboratory responsibilities.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: laboratory record applications can retain selected specimen identity, while culture work, identification and test interpretation remain professional laboratory tasks.

assumptions: Shares are provisional for manual working-record entry after physical microbiology work. OTHER is the laboratory information application. The existing working record is read for result review; no new activity log is introduced.

The technologist verifies specimen identity, protocol, controls, culture dates, observations and findings in s1-s3. Capture and interpretation remain fully counted. Existing accession staff provide identity as part of their normal work, not new free capture.

Native case-context defaults come first. Only 0.5 of 10 repeated specimen-ID entry points is removed; 9.5 retain result entry, identity checks, missing-context repair and ordinary save. Existing automatic context earns no credit; more repair lowers benefits.

s4 is original working-record maintenance, fully human apart from the small specified entry change; its ordinary author save is ungated and earns no saving. Clinical result authorization and outward release are separate actual work and must be added if included in the customer's workflow.
unknowns: Existing specimen context and actual repeated identifier entry
research_questions: Observe microbiology working-record entry and count identity checks separately from repeated typing.

incremental.description: Check specimen-context defaults after record-form changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Remove 0.5 repeated identifier points less 0.2 upkeep. An unusual organism requires a different working form; reuse only 0.3 points of stable specimen identity and retain other entry: 0.3 minus 0.2 = 0.1.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Retain laboratory science, physical microbiology and clinical authority while reducing specified repeat calculations and limited record/procedure restatement.
role.ambitious_version: No autonomous organism identification or clinical method release is proposed.
